proofs.full_local_argument: 1. Relabel the neighboring actions 1,2 and put d=ell_2-ell_1, F=C_1 intersect C_2, B={k:F subset C_k}, D={1,...,N} minus B. Both C_1,C_2 have dimension M-1. For completeness, maximal nonempty cells have this property: take x in relint C_i, approach x by full-support simplex points avoiding all equality hyperplanes of distinct loss rows, and pass to a subsequence with one minimizing action h. C_h is full dimensional and contains x. The affine function (ell_h-ell_i)^T p is nonnegative on C_i and zero at its relative interior point x, hence zero throughout C_i. Thus C_i subset C_h; maximality makes them equal. Duplicate rows do not affect this argument. Neighboring cells are distinct, since equal full-dimensional cells cannot intersect in dimension M-2; therefore d is nonzero and takes both positive and negative values on the simplex. Otherwise one of C_1,C_2 would be properly contained in the other.  2. F has a point in the interior of the simplex. If it did not, convexity and nonnegativity of coordinates imply F lies in a coordinate facet: otherwise averaging, for every coordinate, points of F with that coordinate positive gives a full-support point. That coordinate facet and aff F both have dimension M-2, so they have the same affine hull. Since d^T p=0 on F, d would be a scalar multiple of that coordinate vector, contradicting its two signs on the simplex. Choose p0 in relint F. Every coordinate of p0 is positive, because a nonnegative affine coordinate attaining zero at a relative interior point is zero on all F.  3. For k in B, (ell_k-ell_1)^T p vanishes on F. The linear span of F has dimension M-1: its affine dimension is M-2 and sum_j p_j=1 separates its affine hull from the origin. Its orthogonal complement is therefore spanned by d. Thus ell_k=ell_1+a_k d. Optimality on the full-dimensional cells C_1 and C_2, which contain points with d^T p>0 and d^T p<0 respectively, gives 0<=a_k<=1. This includes a_1=0,a_2=1, duplicates and all degenerate neighborhood actions. For k in D, delta_k=(ell_k-ell_1)^T p0>0: it is nonnegative on F, and zero at p0 would force it to vanish on F and hence put k in B. If D is nonempty let delta=min_{k in D} delta_k>0.  4. Let W=sum_{k in B} im(S_k^T). Since d is outside W, its orthogonal projection w onto W-perp is nonzero and d^T w=||w||_2^2>0. Set v=w/(d^T w). Then d^T v=1 and S_k v=0 for every k in B, not just actions 1 and 2. Every S_k has rows summing to the all-ones row, so sum_j v_j=0. Consequently p_+=p0+epsilon v and p_-=p0-epsilon v are probability vectors for all sufficiently small epsilon>0, with coordinates at least p0_j/2. For k in B their gaps against action 1 under p_+ and action 2 under p_- are exactly a_k epsilon and (1-a_k)epsilon. For k in D choose a fixed epsilon0>0 small enough that both gaps remain at least beta=delta/2. Explicitly impose epsilon0|v_j|<=p0_j/2 for every j, epsilon0|(ell_k-ell_1)^T v|<=delta_k/2 and epsilon0|(ell_k-ell_2)^T v|<=delta_k/2 for every k in D, ignoring zero coefficients. Finite sets and positive p0,delta_k ensure epsilon0>0. These facts also prove p_+ in C_1 and p_- in C_2. If D is empty set beta=1 and omit the D inequalities; the assertions about D are vacuous.  5. For distributions q,r with r positive, log u<=u-1 gives KL(q||r)<=sum_j(q_j-r_j)^2/r_j. Applied to p_+,p_-, this is at most C epsilon^2, with C=8 sum_j v_j^2/p0_j>0, uniformly for epsilon<=epsilon0. Deterministic feedback cannot increase KL: group coordinates by symbol and apply the log-sum inequality, which follows from convexity of u log u with weights proportional to r_j. Thus each action's symbol KL is at most C epsilon^2. For k in B it is exactly zero because S_k v=0.  6. Include the learner's complete private random seed U, sampled independently of outcomes, in the transcript along with actions and feedback through round T. Conditional on U and past feedback, actions are deterministic. The law of U is identical in the two environments, and action factors contribute zero log-likelihood ratio. Factoring the successive feedback probabilities and taking expectation therefore gives KL(P_+||P_-)<=C epsilon^2 n_D^+, where n_D^+ is the expected number of D actions under p_+. This holds after integrating over U, including arbitrary randomized learners, without choosing a hard distribution separately for each deterministic seed. All outcome probabilities are positive, so no support obstruction occurs.  7. Write TV=TV(P_+,P_-). The bound TV<=sqrt(KL(P_+||P_-)/2) can be obtained by taking the event where the P_+ density exceeds the P_- density, applying log-sum on it and its complement, and using binary KL(a||b)>=2(a-b)^2. The latter follows by integrating the second derivative 1/[a(1-a)]>=4 in a from its minimum at a=b; endpoint cases follow by limits. For any transcript statistic Z in [0,T], |E_+ Z-E_- Z|<=T TV, by integrating its level-set probabilities.  8. Define U_B=sum_t a_{I_t}1{I_t in B} and V_B=sum_t(1-a_{I_t})1{I_t in B}; both lie in [0,T] and U_B+V_B=T-N_D pathwise. Let r_+,r_- be expected stochastic regret. Fresh iid outcomes are independent of the selected action conditional on the past and seed, so expected regret is the sum of expected action gaps. The gaps from step 4 imply r_+>=epsilon E_+ U_B+beta n_D^+, r_->=epsilon E_- V_B+beta n_D^-. In particular both regrets are nonnegative and r_++r_->=epsilon(T-n_D^+)-epsilon T TV, dropping only nonnegative costly-action terms.  9. Fix a>0 with a<=epsilon0 and a<=1/(2 sqrt(C)), and set epsilon=a T^(-1/3). If n_D^+>=T^(2/3)/2 then r_+>=beta T^(2/3)/2. Otherwise n_D^+<T^(2/3)/2<=T/2 and KL(P_+||P_-)<=C a^2/2<=1/8, so TV<=1/4. Step 8 gives r_++r_->=epsilon T/4, hence max(r_+,r_-)>=a T^(2/3)/8. Thus c(G)=min(beta/2,a/8)>0 works for every integer T>=1 and every randomized learner. The two perturbed distributions depend only on G,T; selecting the worse one yields the exact assigned quantifier order. No restriction on actions outside B, nondegeneracy assumption, global observability assumption, or extra oracle restriction was introduced.

assumptions: There exists a neighboring pair i,j for which d=ell_j-ell_i is outside the full span sum_{k in B} im(S_k^T).
The learner uses only its own randomness, past actions and chosen-action feedback; no outcome, unchosen-action feedback, side information or additional loss observation is supplied.
statement.conclusion: E[R_T(A,p)]>=c(G)T^(2/3) for some iid outcome distribution p. No nondegeneracy or global observability assumption is added.
statement.objects_and_definitions: Known finite game G=(L,H), N actions, M outcomes, L in [0,1]^(N by M), and arbitrary distinguishable feedback symbols H. Write ell_k for loss row k as a column, Delta_M={p>=0:sum_j p_j=1}, C_k={p in Delta_M:ell_k^T p<=ell_h^T p for every h}. Dominated means C_k empty; degenerate means nonempty C_k properly contained in some C_h; Pareto-optimal means neither. Duplicate loss rows are allowed and are not removed. Neighbors i,j are Pareto-optimal actions with dim(C_i intersect C_j)=M-2. Set F=C_i intersect C_j and B={k:F subset C_k}, including every action with this property. S_k has one row for each distinct symbol in feedback row k and entry (a,j)=1{H_kj equals symbol a}. Local observability of this pair means ell_j-ell_i belongs to sum_{k in B} im(S_k^T). At round t the learner chooses I_t before the fresh outcome J_t and receives only H_{I_t,J_t}. Define R_T(A,p)=sum_t L_{I_t,J_t}-T min_k ell_k^T p for iid J_t with law p.
statement.parameter_domains: Finite positive integers N,M; the neighboring-pair premise implies M>=2. Every integer T>=1. Constants may depend on the entire fixed game, not on A or T.
statement.quantifiers_and_randomness: For each fixed such G there exists c(G)>0 such that for every adaptive randomized learner A and every integer T>=1 there exists p=p(A,T) in Delta_M for which E[R_T(A,p)]>=c(G)T^(2/3). Expectation includes learner randomness and iid outcomes. In fact the proof uses a pair p_+(T),p_-(T) fixed independently of A, one of which is hard for A.
